notes.body:
There are a few comments in the code saying this is desired, but I'm looking for feedback on the architecture of it.
- Should there be a wsutil_init/cleanup that houses the "value string init/cleanup"?
- What should qualify to put a value_string in wsutil?
- Was the DISSECTOR_ASSERT functionality properly ported?
- Should the value_string_ext functionality have its own wmem scope (instead of NULL)

> Was the DISSECTOR_ASSERT functionality properly ported?

Some of the `ws_warn_badarg` calls should probably be `ws_return_val_if` or `ws_return_str_if` calls that return something. The interesting question, I guess, is because in a lot of the cases the parameter that shouldn't be NULL is only used in the "value wasn't found in the value_string" case, whether it should return immediately if the fmt/constant is NULL or only if it's necessary.

The intention of the external_value_string API was to just abstract the explicit linking of value_strings defined in dissectors but used by the GUI.  Previously, if the value_string was "spelled wrong", you'd get a compile or linking error (so no runtime error possible).  Now because of the extra layer, I'd still like it to be as punitive as possible at runtime if there's a spelling mistake in the name string passed in so it's fixed immediately.

There were definitely some challenges when APIs want a value_string returned instead of a string when checking for "developer errors", because this is where ws_warn_badarg doesn't really work in Release builds like DISSECTOR_ASSERT would when value_string functionality was in epan.

DISSECTOR_ASSERT throws an exception, which stops the current packet from being dissected, doesn't crash Wireshark.

`ws_warn_badarg` is just a console warning, and might still crash.
`ws_return_val_if` and `ws_return_str_if` are console warnings, and return a legal value, though that only happens in Debug enabled builds (and probably still crash in Release builds.) If the calculation isn't painfully slow, we can do the test regardless and return a value on failure.

We just don't really have access to the exception handling from wsutil.

And with the lack of access to the exception handling, I feel the options are closer to "silent fails" or "harder to find developer bugs".  Do you think more use of ws_return_val_if and ws_return_str_if should have phrases like "BAD value_string, no donut!" (only less humorous) so that the string shows up in the dissection like the DISSECTOR_ASSERT functions can do?

Well, the first thing is that DISSECTOR_ASSERT currently doesn't entirely crash Wireshark, unless the CRASH_ON_DISSECTOR_BUG or whatever environment variable is set.

These, right now possibly crash (on some OSes) because of accessing NULLs with string functions, at least in the "the value isn't in the value_string so let's fallback to either a constant string or printf" case. (Though GNU libc and others will just merrily substitute "<NULL>" or similar in some cases.)

So the first question is, should Wireshark entirely crash in those cases?
A second question is, should Wireshark entirely crash on just Release builds (optimized) but on Debug builds have assert checks that only crash if we ask it to crash?

But aside from that I do think that it would be useful to have an error message (with the string) show up in the dissection itself somehow since some people don't pay attention to console warnings.

(Both comments seem to be around the same general area of issues of migrating DISSECTOR_ASSERT -> ws_warn_badarg/ws_warning).  I gave it another shot with the latest commit, let me know what you think.

> Should the value_string_ext functionality have its own wmem scope (instead of NULL)

I think that the non-static (not used much) functionality of `value_string_ext_new` should probably take a scope as an argument. The free function could I guess stay the same if the scope is saved as a new member of the `value_string_ext`. (It could be NULL for the static ones, just people should never, ever call `value_string_ext_free()` on a static vse.)
Done

commits_data.title: Move value_string functionality to wsutil
commits_data.message:
Move value_string functionality to wsutil

1. Rename vs_get_external_value_string -> get_external_value_string (as it was missed during the initial review of adding that new functionality)
2. Add wmem scope argument to val[64]_string_ext_new and save the scope for freeing later.
